land.text: Anga 'between the Champa river to the west and the Rajmahal hills to the east', capital 'at the confluence of the Champa and Ganga rivers' near Bhagalpur and Malini near Munger; the same shape as the janapada-of-anga dossier (sa-01-a)

successors.note: The same state: the sa-01-a dossier starts in -600 with Cliopatria's Anga row and ends in -530 when Bimbisara of Magadha kills Brahmadatta. One hue for the chain (rule 2).

capitals.name: Champa (Champapuri, near Bhagalpur)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Champapuri (near modern Bhagalpur) and Malini (near modern Munger), Bihar'; Campa 'at the confluence of the Champa and Ganga rivers'. The page dates neither seat; Malini is a second seat. Coordinates are the town's.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria's Janapada of Anga row is -600..-501). Infobox 'Established: Unknown (~1100 BCE)', 'Disestablished: c. 530 BCE'. The infobox gives no area; the shape is the janapada-of-anga shape, about 15,000 km2.

region.text: Anga 'between the Champa river to the west and the Rajmahal hills to the east', capital 'at the confluence of the Champa and Ganga rivers' near Bhagalpur and Malini near Munger; the same shape as the janapada-of-anga dossier (sa-01-a)

ledger.note: c. 1100 BCE: the kingdom of Anga stands on the middle Ganges. Infobox 'Established: Unknown (~1100 BCE)', 'Historical era: Iron Age', 'Aṅga and other kingdoms of the late Vedic period'. The page dates nothing else before the 6th century, so the whole early life is traditional.

region.text: Anga 'between the Champa river to the west and the Rajmahal hills to the east', capital 'at the confluence of the Champa and Ganga rivers' near Bhagalpur and Malini near Munger; the same shape as the janapada-of-anga dossier (sa-01-a)

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: the Anga of the Vedic and Jain tradition becomes the janapada of Anga. The page has no event for the date; it is the Mahajanapada convention year of the sa-01-a dossier, and 'During the 6th century BCE, the king of Anga was Dadhivahana'. Bimbisara's conquest ('in the middle of the 6th century BCE', infobox 'c. 530 BCE') is that dossier's.

certainty.note: A late-Vedic kingdom; the page gives rivers and hills for 'Anga proper', and its dates are infobox dates.

sources.title: Anga
sources.note: Infobox (~1100 BCE to c. 530 BCE, capitals Champapuri and Malini, succeeded by Magadha), Anga proper between the Champa river and the Rajmahal hills, Dadhivahana, Brahmadatta and Bimbisara.

notes: Written from the Anga infobox date that sa-01-a did not draw (their notes: 'Anga ~1100'). The page dates nothing between ~1100 and the 6th century, so the dossier is two events and one shape. The Anga page also says the kingdom had 'at times' included Magadha in the west and Vanga, and extended to the sea: no date, not drawn. Kalinga's capture of Dadhivahana is the sa-01-a dossier's note (Kalinga appears in the counterpart list).
